title: How would 1345 look if we count only by fives?
description: A system that counts only in groups of five needs one symbol for every group. The video divides 1345 by 5 to find how many symbols are needed, and checks the count by putting the groups back. Keeko's doubt is that fives make the row short.
teaching_notes: One idea: a single group size gives a very long row for a big number, so it soon becomes cumbersome. The count of group symbols is the number divided by the group size. Watch for students who expect a short row just because the group is bigger than one.

source: In a system that counts only by 5s, how would 1345 be writte

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, find how many fives make one thousand three hundred forty five.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Divide by five. That gives two hundred sixty nine.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: check: 269 × 5 = 200 × 5 + 60 × 5 + 9 × 5 = 1000 + 300 + 45 = 1345, so nothing is left over

marks.m3: the parts 1000, 300 and 45 are added to give 1345, with nothing left over

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, put the groups back to check.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two hundred fives make one thousand. Sixty fives make three hundred. Nine fives make forty five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Together they make one thousand three hundred forty five, so nothing is left over.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 1345 needs the symbol for five written 269 times

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, write the number.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>One thousand three hundred forty five needs the symbol for five written two hundred sixty nine times.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: that is far too many symbols to write or read, so one group size alone soon becomes cumbersome

<bookmark mark='m5'/>That is far too many symbols to write or to read. A single group size soon becomes cumbersome.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 269 symbols for five, too many to write or read easily
